questions.e: 'Individuals and interactions over processes and tools' is about respect for people — trusting team members, respecting their autonomy, and fostering open, honest communication; it is an ethical statement about the dignity of human beings.

questions.q: The Agile value 'Working software' is framed as an ethical commitment to:
o: quality and usefulness — not taking shortcuts that compromise performance or security
questions.e: Delivering working software isn't just about functionality; it's about not compromising on quality and not taking shortcuts that could affect performance or security — an ethical commitment to quality and usefulness.

questions.q: The ethical dilemma 'Quality versus Speed' arises when:
o: a tight timeline tempts the team to cut corners to deliver on time versus upholding quality
the team has too much time
questions.e: Quality versus Speed is the dilemma of whether to cut corners to deliver on time or uphold quality (risking the deadline); the suggested solution is open communication/transparency with stakeholders to negotiate scope, deadlines or resources.

questions.q: The suggested solution to the 'Honesty versus Fear of Conflict' dilemma is:
o: fostering a psychologically safe environment where members can voice concerns without fear, with leaders modeling openness
questions.e: The solution to Honesty versus Fear of Conflict is fostering a psychologically safe environment where team members feel safe to voice concerns without fear of criticism; leaders model openness and emphasize learning over blame.

questions.q: The Agile principle that resolves the 'Customer Satisfaction versus Employee Well-being' dilemma is:
o: sustainable pace — balancing productivity and rest with realistic expectations
questions.e: Sustainable pace, one of Agile's principles, resolves the Customer Satisfaction versus Employee Well-being dilemma by striking a balance between productivity and rest, setting realistic expectations and nurturing self-care.

questions.q: Which real-world scandal is cited as an example of unethical behavior damaging customer trust through misuse of user data?
questions.e: The Facebook–Cambridge Analytica scandal (2018) — where Facebook exposed millions of users' data without consent to a political consulting firm — is cited as a stark example of a breach of trust damaging customer trust and raising ethical questions.

questions.q: The Theranos scandal (Elizabeth Holmes) is used to illustrate the impact of unethical behavior on:
o: product quality — misleading investors, manipulating test results and delivering inaccurate diagnoses
questions.e: The Theranos example (Elizabeth Holmes' blood-testing company) illustrates unethical practices affecting product quality — misleading investors, manipulating test results and delivering inaccurate diagnoses — leading to the company's downfall.

questions.q: Which is recommended for fostering an ethical culture in Agile teams?
o: lead with values — leaders exemplify Agile values and demonstrate ethical behavior through actions
questions.e: Fostering an ethical culture includes: lead with values (leaders exemplify openness, respect, courage, commitment and focus), set clear expectations, encourage open dialogue, emphasize learning over blame, reward ethical behavior, and embed ethics in decision-making.

questions.q: 'Emphasize Learning over Blame' as an ethical-culture practice means:
o: treating ethical missteps (often from lack of understanding) as opportunities for learning rather than occasions for blame
questions.e: Emphasize Learning over Blame: ethical missteps are often not ill intent but a lack of understanding; when they occur, use them as opportunities for learning — discuss implications, explore alternatives, and cultivate continuous improvement.

questions.q: The 'Four-Way Test' (originated by Rotary International) asks whether something is the TRUTH, is FAIR to all, will build goodwill, and:
o: will be beneficial to all concerned
questions.e: The Four-Way Test asks four questions about the things we think, say or do: Is it the TRUTH? Is it FAIR to all concerned? Will it build GOODWILL and BETTER FRIENDSHIPS? Will it be BENEFICIAL to all concerned?

questions.q: Kant's Categorical Imperative, as an ethical decision-making framework, suggests you should:
o: act only according to a maxim you could will to become a universal law (if you're comfortable with everyone doing it, it's likely ethical)
questions.e: Kant's Categorical Imperative says to 'act only according to that maxim whereby you can at the same time will that it should become a universal law' — if you're comfortable with everyone else doing what you're about to do, it's likely ethical.

questions.q: The Utilitarian approach (attributed to Bentham and Mill) advocates:
o: choosing the action that maximizes overall happiness or minimizes overall pain
questions.e: The Utilitarian approach, attributed to Jeremy Bentham and John Stuart Mill, advocates choosing the action that maximizes overall happiness or minimizes overall pain — for Agile teams, prioritizing user needs and balancing stakeholder interests.

questions.q: The Ethical OS Toolkit (developed by the Institute for the Future and Omidyar Network) helps teams:
o: anticipate the future impact and unintended consequences of their products across eight risk zones
questions.e: The Ethical OS Toolkit helps tech teams anticipate future impact and unintended consequences of their products; it provides prompts, checklists and scenarios spanning eight risk zones (e.g. Truth/Disinformation, Addiction & the Dopamine Economy).
